Serializes, updates, and reads the recent blockhashes sysvar from the bank queue.

# Purpose
This file manages the `recent blockhashes` sysvar account for a bank. It builds the account data from the bank blockhash queue, writes that data into the sysvar account, and reads the account back into a decoded `fd_recent_block_hashes_t` object. The main data path is [`encode_rbh_from_blockhash_queue`](<#encode_rbh_from_blockhash_queue>), which copies the queue size and then serializes up to `FD_SYSVAR_RECENT_HASHES_CAP` entries, each entry containing a 32-byte hash and a fee value. [`fd_sysvar_recent_hashes_init`](<#fd_sysvar_recent_hashes_init>) uses that encoding to create the sysvar account, and [`fd_sysvar_recent_hashes_update`](<#fd_sysvar_recent_hashes_update>) first registers the current PoH hash in the queue and then refreshes the account data.

The file also defines the read path for the sysvar. [`fd_sysvar_recent_hashes_read`](<#fd_sysvar_recent_hashes_read>) loads the account from `funk`, checks that the account exists and has lamports, computes the decode footprint, allocates memory from `spad`, and decodes the account data into a `fd_recent_block_hashes_t` object. The code uses direct serialization and decode helpers from the sysvar and account manager layers, and it exposes a narrow interface for init, update, and read operations on `fd_sysvar_recent_block_hashes_id`.
